fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Quality Comes First, Quantity Follows", "body": "After years of chasing output, Chance Garton describes flipping his whole operating premise: the Iron Age mindset he calls the Kali Yuga insists that stuff, broken into small enough particles, generates qualities, the same logic that says wet brain meat manufactures consciousness or that an alloy's elemental makeup grants it conductivity. Garton argues the arrow runs the other way, that physical matter condenses out of qualities existing prior to and regardless of any material, so quality creates quantity. Wann, freshly out of eight or nine months of hermit mode, applies the same test to his own work, asking only whether it feels right."}, {"title": "Pattern Recognition as a Practice", "body": "Garton makes his living hitting tuning forks, reading information out of the human energy field, which he describes as having an anatomy as consistent from person to person as the placement of heart and lungs. Sessions become pattern hunts: he locates stuck energy at a coordinate, offers a rough shape of the story, a memory surfaces, then another lands twenty years later on the same timeline with identical circumstances. He recounts a tiny woman with severe post-meal bloating who had to wear loose clothing, whose real grief was regret over not having more children. Information is not wisdom, he insists; wisdom is patterns."}, {"title": "The Dungeon Master and the Engineered Vibe Shift", "body": "Wann and Garton nickname whoever runs this realm the Dungeon Master, a figure with a wicked sense of humor who tells you your brain is built to see patterns and then tells you not to trust the patterns you see. Wann notes the clue hidden in that contradiction. Garton describes his own tell: during the early lockdown panic he sat with roughly two minutes of terror before realizing he was not actually afraid to die, and the fear was not his. Years later, watching a widely circulated assassination clip, he felt the same imported dread arrive through a screen and dropped it."}, {"title": "Snake Eyes, Star Trek, and Plausible Deniability", "body": "Wann traces a five-month arc through his own videos, from the Texas flooding to Kiss Cam Gate to the birth and homicide at Burning Man, all of it feeding into the Charlie Kirk story. The moment he hit publish, the 1998 Brian De Palma film Snake Eyes surfaced publicly, and Wann argues its overlaps are so exact they feel manufactured rather than organic. Garton counters with Star Trek season one, episode two, aired September 15, 1966, where Captain Kirk teaches an isolated young man named Charlie about gender and threatens his neck. Wann's rule: real synchronicity keeps plausible deniability, contrivance does not."}, {"title": "Hyperreality, Egregores, and the Burning Man Sequence", "body": "Garton brings in Jean Baudrillard's Simulacra and Simulation, the hollowed-out book Neo uses in The Matrix, to define hyperreality: a media-built worldview so absorbing that actual life outside the window starts feeling unreal. His conclusion is that nine competing fake-out theories all wave the same flag, that the screen itself is not the thing. Wann adds that projected belief still builds egregores, something from nothing. He stacks the August 29, 2025 sequence, BlackRock's chief named interim WEF head a week before a festival held at Black Rock City, a so-called cryptic birth, a first homicide, and Pluto going out of bounds."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: What if your birth chart isn’t a symbol of fate, but a map of where you are in the living cosmos? Michael Wann returns to InnerVerse to explore astrology as orientation, not fortune-telling, showing how time itself is a landscape we inhabit. Together, we uncover how cosmic timing, personal holy days, and celestial bearings can ground consciousness in the eternal now.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: From the spaghetti strands of modern media illusion to the sky’s original geometry of meaning, this dialogue is a reminder: the heavens are not out there, they’re your coordinates of being.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Chiron and Systems That Talk Back", "body": "Chance explains that Chiron, a body only recently discovered and named the wounded healer, describes people's most common emotional wound so precisely that he uses it as his metric for choosing between tropical and sidereal and between house systems. He dismisses the idea that astrology was invented by farmers timing their harvests and proposes instead that complex, circular systems of correspondence yield more than was encoded into them, like two notes producing a harmonic. Mike answers that his course runs case studies on Chiron and on Pluto, and frames astrology as hypnotic anchoring on the sky across thousands of generations."}, {"title": "The Dungeon Master's Real Job", "body": "Returning to the Dungeons and Dragons metaphor, Chance argues that a good campaign needs immersion, which means the dungeon master has to genuinely scare you and make you worry about your character. By that logic the demiurge is not out to ruin or control your life but to manufacture conflict and threat so the game feels real. He wonders aloud whether explaining this spoils the game, then allows that some people need the boogeyman while others can play pretend on purpose. Mike says the work they are doing together is helping people become un-immersed, not to leave the game but to recognize it is one."}, {"title": "The Zodiac as a Clock", "body": "Mike describes how his own astrology has moved away from subjective interpretation toward objective timing, treating the chart as a timing mechanism. He calls the zodiac, inherited from the Babylonian priest class that also produced taxation and social classes, a beautiful calendar: 360 degrees against a 365 day solar cycle, the sun advancing a degree a day and changing signs around the 21st of each month. The ascendant is the eastern horizon, so the sun sits there at dawn and at the midheaven at noon. Chance adds that he uses astrology in hindsight to prove his life is in sync, shifting paranoia into pronoia."}, {"title": "Personal Holy Days", "body": "Mike introduces a practice he invented called personal holy days. Translate the degree and sign of your ascendant into the calendar date when the sun reaches it, which for Chance's Leo rising falls in late July, and be awake at sunrise that day, which Mike calls the day of becoming. Repeat it for the descendant, midheaven, IC and the nodes, eight dates a year of being present. Chance connects it to his Chiron in Cancer in the eleventh house: once he took his outsider feeling as a perspective rather than a reality, he was invited within the week to speak at the festival he had felt shut out of."}, {"title": "Bearings in Time and Space", "body": "Mike argues that humanity's purest relationship with the heavens is bearings: the sky is the one thing everyone can see equally, and it tells you where you are and what time of year it is, never what to do. Chance compares the versions of astrology to the countless maps of Missouri, each useful and none real, while Mike insists a chart is an accurate schematic of the sky and being born at sunrise is not an interpretation. Mike warns that astrologers without this grounding end up floating in the woo, and Chance closes on why he does not fear death: non-existence is nonexistent."}]

fields.Plus Quotes JSON: [{"text": "I think that the job of the demiurge or dungeon master, if you want to call it that, is not to actually ruin your life or control you.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "What are you and I doing right now is we are helping people to become un-immersed, but still recognize, not to leave the game, but to recognize it's a freaking game.", "author": "Michael Wann", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/b7e0ef5f-142f-46eb-a25f-b387285ea071/MICHAEL-WANN.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "In my journey with astrology, it has moved almost completely away, or at least majorly devalued subjective interpretation and really understanding objective timing and understanding your chart as a timing mechanism.", "author": "Michael Wann", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/b7e0ef5f-142f-46eb-a25f-b387285ea071/MICHAEL-WANN.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "I use astrology more as a hindsight device to constantly prove to myself that my life is in perfect sync with everything else happening in all life all the time.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "When you begin to recognize the degrees and the signs are important because they tell you moments of time. Not moments of meaning, moments of time.", "author": "Michael Wann", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/b7e0ef5f-142f-46eb-a25f-b387285ea071/MICHAEL-WANN.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Tomorrow will likely happen, yes, and there is a linear measurable way, the lag of events, but the moment of now is really the only thing that matters.", "author": "Michael Wann", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/b7e0ef5f-142f-46eb-a25f-b387285ea071/MICHAEL-WANN.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "The truest, purest relationship that humanity, like any human being has with the heavens, is that of bearings.", "author": "Michael Wann", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/b7e0ef5f-142f-46eb-a25f-b387285ea071/MICHAEL-WANN.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Each one of these versions of astrology is a map. Just like there's a billion different maps of the state of Missouri.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "If you don't have a solid beginning or founding, well, then you're just floating. You're floating in the woo.", "author": "Michael Wann", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/b7e0ef5f-142f-46eb-a25f-b387285ea071/MICHAEL-WANN.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "There's no reason to actually be afraid of dying, because you can't not exist, because non-existence is nonexistent.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}]
fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "In reality, there is no counterculture. There are only cults and there are free minds. And there's a cult for everyone as long as they're willing to outsource their thinking and beliefs to somebody else.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "That's the only honest truth, is that we don't know. That doesn't mean don't have beliefs. This is just being honest in where you stand with it.", "author": "Michael Wann", "portrait": ""}, {"text": "Information is not wisdom. Let's just get to the simple core of things, because wisdom is patterns.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "I don't know if this literally is a dream. I don't know who's dreaming it. I don't know where it is. We are incapable of knowing that if we're in here.", "author": "Michael Wann", "portrait": ""}, {"text": "When I feel my emotional body shift from an external source in a dramatic way, I've become aware that that's my clue that this is being engineered in some way.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "The best types of these synchronicities through mainstream media have to have at least a good amount of plausible deniability built into it.", "author": "Michael Wann", "portrait": ""}, {"text": "You're getting many flags waved at you. This is fake, this is fake, this is fake. Does it matter which way it's fake, or does it matter that you stop and go, this isn't real?", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "All you care about, if you wanna understand what's happening, is what is being presented to the masses. It has nothing to do with what actually happens. It's what is being told in your hypnosis.", "author": "Michael Wann", "portrait": ""}]
fields.Title: You Are Here: Reading the Map of Time with Michael Wann
